text:
The low thrum had become a part of the air he breathed, a constant, low-frequency pressure behind his eyes. It was a day for things to stop working, David thought, as the ancient microfilm reader sputtered, the image of a forgotten deed flickering erratically. The archives, usually bustling with the ghosts of municipal busywork, felt hollow, hushed, as if the town itself had collectively decided to hold its breath. A faint chill seeped into the room, not from an open window, but from the very bones of the building, a cold that hinted at something deeper than mere temperature. He pressed the feed button, urging the reader forward, a new focus now overriding the vague unease.

Then he saw it. Buried deep in a ledger detailing expenses for the lighthouse’s ‘renovation’ under Elias Thorne’s company, was a single, handwritten entry, almost perfectly camouflaged in the faded ink: "Consultancy fee, L. Huang, 7,625.74." The name, no longer a ghost word on a dying frequency, but solid black ink, stared back at him from the page. The numbers, too, felt familiar, a skewed echo of the persistent 'sevens' that plagued Blackwood Bay, a new permutation in a calculation he still didn't understand. Thorne wasn't just pulling strings; he was unraveling the very fabric of the town, one silent, meticulously recorded transaction at a time. The hum intensified, a deeper vibration now, not just from the earth, but from the paper itself, a resonant frequency that promised more than just a financial scandal.
